5.Discussion 
In this section, three important aspects of the literature behind the 
triage procedure and priority contexts, namely, motivations, challenges, 
and limitations of using AI and recommendations, are discussed to 
mitigate these difficulties to improve triage and prioritisation of 
patients 5.1 Motivations for ASD triage and prioritisation 
This section discusses the advantages of triage and prioritisation 
reported in the academic literature Three main benefits can be identi -
fied from the collected articles as follows: 
≡The triage and prioritisation concepts can reduce cost and time 
consumption to provide an early diagnosis for autism patients The 
conventional clinical diagnosis of autism using ADOS requires be-
tween 60 and 90 min for initial DSM-IV-TR assessment, due to 
variation in reliability between residents [16] and the ADI-R 
assessment of autistic symptoms Each patient needs more than 2 h 
to complete the triage and/or priority process For this, the authors of 
[26] applied “top-ranking items for ASD diagnosis in the Korean 
population ” and can reduce the time to ASD diagnosis They pro-
duced 10 levels of patient prioritisation based on two board-certified 
child psychiatrist triage where they used ADI-R, ADOS and clinical 
interviews Also, the long waiting time for service, clinical appoint -
ments and higher costs are improved Accordingly, several studies 
attempted to overcome these issues to reduce the cost and time 
consumption for diagnosis To overcome the expensive and time 
consumption in the process of genetic and genomic studies were 
usually performed to identify ASD risk genes and numerous gener -
ated potentials nominated genes, and difficulty in validation as well Therefore, a study [12] constructed a predictive model that could 
promote the diagnosis of autism and prioritised cell-type-specificity 
that could be used as potential biomarkers of ASD

To overcome the expensive and time 
consumption in the process of genetic and genomic studies were 
usually performed to identify ASD risk genes and numerous gener -
ated potentials nominated genes, and difficulty in validation as well Therefore, a study [12] constructed a predictive model that could 
promote the diagnosis of autism and prioritised cell-type-specificity 
that could be used as potential biomarkers of ASD The machine 
learning algorithms can identify and predict the genes involved in 
the disorder better than depending only on unclear traditional ge-
netics that consume time in diagnosis [32] Understanding the as-
sociation of genes related to the disorder/disease aids better 
diagnosis and treatments which is better than costly experiments and 
time-consuming during the evaluation of the genes [15] Triage 
process for children with ASD can help sooner by referring them to 
clinical appointments for ASD evaluation and can reduce the wait 
times for both types of children (who have the ASD risk and one’s 
non ASD risk) [10,27,35] In conclusion to the above benefits from 
reducing cost and time consumption, the triage and priority can 
identify ASD risk and nominated genes, leverage machine learning in 
reducing time and cost during ASD diagnosis, and understand the 
association of genes related to the disorder to obtain diagnosis ≡The triage and prioritisation can improve therapeutic strategies and 
aid autism patients with daily activities Determining “the brain 
temporospatial regions where the risk genes are expressed in ASD 
patients ” could improve the therapeutic strategies for better 
healthcare and treatment for ASD risky patients [34] Besides, 
releasing the association of genes for ASD patients through priority 
tools helps in designing therapeutic strategies and better diagnostic 
situations [15]

level0_chunks.content:
Determining “the brain 
temporospatial regions where the risk genes are expressed in ASD 
patients ” could improve the therapeutic strategies for better 
healthcare and treatment for ASD risky patients [34] Besides, 
releasing the association of genes for ASD patients through priority 
tools helps in designing therapeutic strategies and better diagnostic 
situations [15] ≡Triage and prioritisation focusing on autism case evaluations, which 
are important to identify the appropriate treatment for patients and 
prioritise the certain patients considered ‘urgent ’ than other ASD 
patients with less symptoms The evaluation of the status of each ASD 
patient, which prompts the clinicians to consider and implement 
diagnostic processes innovatively to adapt the situation and serve the 
patients ’ need,is essential during Covid-19 and any pandemics [9] 5.2 Challenges for ASD triage and prioritisation 
Several concerns detailed in studies related to diagnosis, prioritising 
and triage patients are shown in (Fig 6) The identification of all risky 
genes that contribute to ASD risk are still concerning, and no standard 
set of risky genes has been identified [15,29,32] Although many studies 
attempted to determine them, they overlook potentially instrumental 
mutations with small to medium effect sizes [3] No laboratory of neu-
roimaging tests or even any biochemical markers can currently be uti-
lised as a diagnostic standard for ASD [4] “The causal variants and the 
specific cell types in which the diseases-risk variants may be active are 
unclear ” [12] A strong clue of clinical and genetic overlap was observed 
between ASD and other types of neurodevelopmental disorders and 
represented by a spectrum of disorders, such as overlapping with epi-
lepsy or high-functioning autism [2,31] The age of patients that is 
covered has a gap due to the limited available data for ages including 
31–48 months of age [35] However, the evidence level of using EEG 
monitoring has not yet reached the recommended level for diagnostic or 
even screening of all ASD [5]

31–48 months of age [35] However, the evidence level of using EEG 
monitoring has not yet reached the recommended level for diagnostic or 
even screening of all ASD [5] The improvement of identification of ASD 
earlier is still concerning for clinical, besides, the limitation of ASD 
clinicians, causes overwhelming, due to the volume of referrals, thereby 
enabling patients to get much time until evaluations [27] The prioriti -
sation may vary according to the availability of human equipment and 
resources, as well as some policies that are sensitive to domestic prob-
lems in contrast to the goal of ASD evaluations [9] In conclusion, four 
main challenges were encountered: there is an ambiguity of identifica -
tion of risk genes, and the overlapping with other neurodevelopmental 
disorders could be an open issue The data limitations are still a valid 
concern, especially for the lack of medical and laboratory data, besides 
the issues of early diagnosis and poor supplementary services (Fig 6) 5.3 Recommendations for ASD triage and prioritisation 
This section illustrates the recommendations of all collected studies 
that are related to the prioritisation and triage concepts, as well as 
several future opportunities to evaluate the tools related to ASD, 
including studies for improving the accuracy of standard assessment 
tools ≡Recommendations to implement the proposed models : Some 
studies constructed predictive models for autistic diagnosis and 
others ranked their results, such as prioritised finding risky genes and 
recommended to replicate their finding for future work Researchers 
mentioned their constructed predictive models for promoting the 
diagnosis of ASD and may use the “cell type-specific ASD-associated 
genes and gene sets” as prospective biomarkers of ASD [12]

≡Recommendation to investigate ASD risky genes: According to 
literature, no specific risky gene set finding is attained yet, but 
several studies had classified some genes as risky and contributed in 
autism In Ref [31], the authors recommended further investigating 
needs in the future to determine whether their ranked gene system 
can be specified only for ASD The study of [32] focused on 
“developing and validating statistical models for genetic association, 
specifically for the association between rare variants and disease ”, to 
discover illness genes ≡Recommendations to utilize AI for ASD diagnosis : The AI can 
provide a quick diagnosis in medical science before the final diag-
nostic, which depends on expert decision [26] The use of sophisti -
cated modelling and learning algorithms is highly recommended to 
remarkably describe the genetic architecture of complicated disor -
ders and diseases [12,15] ≡Recommendations for data availability: The data limitation can 
slow down the development of research in specific fields The “high- 
quality gene expression profiles ” must be more available publicly in 
the future to facilitate accurate developing models for autism risk 
gene prediction [30,34] 6.ASD: critical analysis and research gaps 
This study conducts a comprehensive analysis of scientific mapping 
and discusses current state and open issues that aid in the imple -
mentation and improvement of the recommended solution of the ASD 
research direction No clear identification of the contribution of AI, 
intelligent decision-making and machine learning is provided to eval-
uate and prioritise autism patients according to their health severity However, most studies have only focused on prioritising risk genes, and 
no clear method has been applied to assign proper weights to gene types 
or even to identify influential genes in the context of intelligent decision- 
making methods

level0_chunks.content:
No clear identification of the contribution of AI, 
intelligent decision-making and machine learning is provided to eval-
uate and prioritise autism patients according to their health severity However, most studies have only focused on prioritising risk genes, and 
no clear method has been applied to assign proper weights to gene types 
or even to identify influential genes in the context of intelligent decision- 
making methods The integration of medical tests and demographic 
criteria can play a vital role in the detection of triage severity levels, and 
minimal attention has been paid to the prioritisation solution for the 
autism patients In addition, no attempts have been made to develop a 
clinical triage method for ASD patients Five complex and important 
open issues associated with the current topic of this study are stated in 
this section 6.1 Available ASD datasets and resources 
Several studies have focused on prioritising ASD-risk genes based on 
the online dataset (SFARI Genes) that classified many genes associated with autism, that is, from high-confidence genes to syndrome Other 
studies focused on examining ASD patients according to clinical diag-
nostic measures, such as ADOS and ADI-R [26,27] or by using EEG [5] to 
collect data (Table 2) As shown in Table 2, the studies of [3,15,29–32] used SFARI genes as 
high confidence In Ref [14], the study used 65 reported genes from 
Ref [36] In addition, the true negative genes from non-ASD genes were 
created by Ref [37], and these genes were related to non-mental dis-
eases In Ref [32], the study has also used the second high-confidence 
ASD risky gene set compiled from three extensive Transmission and 
De Novo Association Analysis (TADA) studies [36,39,40] The study of 
[29] added 1000 genes that are not listed in the SAFRI gene database as 
negative examples In Ref

conclusion, 10 out of 12 studies have been focused on gene datasets These studies are depending on either genetic or social databases ASD refers to a mental disorder It can also have social aetiologies Thus, a sociodemographic dataset that consists of medical and social 
criteria that influence ASD have not been used in terms of triage and 
priority for autism patients The affected criteria that can be used for 
ASD needs more investigation In addition, no study uses medical and 
laboratory test criteria for the triage and prioritisation of patients [10, 
26] Laboratory and clinical data, such as D3, B12, Zinc, T3, T4, TSH, 
GSE, patient ’s blood type, maternal blood type and father ’s blood group, 
need to be considered [42,43] 6.2 Application of used traditional machine learnings and deep learning 
AI science is implemented with multidisciplinary studies that aid to 
build more precise results Thus, several articles in autism utilised ma-
chine learning methods (Table 3) Study [3] trained and optimized five different ML models: SVM with 
linear kernel, RF, extremely randomized trees, bagging ensemble of RF 
and AdaBoost ensemble of RF The training approach consisted of 
stratified fivefold cross-validation with a nested grid-search In 
Ref [30], different ML algorithms, including SVM, RF and logistic 
regression (LR), were tested The developmental brain gene expression 
profiles and RNA transcript sequence compositions were used as features 
for model construction to predict and prioritise ASD-associated candi -

most severe case and ranking other patients are required In these con-

tients and providing the suitable healthcare services from medical 
centres or hospitals 6.3 Gene contributions towards machine learning 
Gene is a basic functional and physical unit of inheritance where 
deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) was represented as a molecular repository 
of genes that encodes the structure of a gene product, either RNA or 
protein [57] Meanwhile, a gene mutation corresponds to a modification 
in one or more genes Some mutations can lead to genetic disorders or 
illnesses [58] Therefore, many scholars researched the effectiveness of 
genes and mutations on ASD The ASD is extremely heritable with the 
association of several genetic syndromes, such as ‘Fragile X and Rett 
syndrome ’ [4] Accordingly, several studies found that the de novo or 
transmitted loss of function (LOF) mutations could disrupt 
protein-coding genes and were regarded as ASD aetiology [30] Several 
studies leverage machine learning approaches for prioritising 
high-confidence gene candidates in ASD The enhanced implementation 
of effective interventions to predict the highest confidence gene sets that 
affect ASD [12] Accordingly, AI tools and methods play a vital role in 
revealing many risky genes that may contribute to ASD [59] According 
to the literature, several ML methods had been used to distinguish the 
risk genes of ASD (Table 4) As shown in Table 4, each of the mentioned studies had produced a 
top-ranked ASD gene set by using known ML approaches to identify and 
prioritise the genes of ASD All listed studies above had attempted to 
label genes into risk and non-risk genes by using several ML methods, 
such as SVM, RF and LR

level0_chunks.content:
Gap analysis directions 
This study aims to show the importance of prioritisation based on 
specific triage for patients who suffer from ASD and how AI can aid in 
this field The literature that are collected on the basis our taxonomy can 
offer certain advantages Firstly, most of the collected studies focused on 
reducing cost and time consumption, which are important for early 
diagnosis to help families from waiting a long time to be served [10,12, 
15,26,27,32,35] Meanwhile, another study focused on improving 
therapeutic strategy, which is essential for enhancing the healthcare of 
patients [34,60,61] The evaluation of autism patients is important for 
their prioritisation according to the urgency of their needs where triaged 
based on specialists decisions [9] The study also showed some concern 
according to literature The diagnosis of autism remains challenging 
itself due to highly overlapping ASD with other neurodevelopmental 
disorders, such as high-functioning autism and epilepsy [2,31] Another 
concern is the limitation of data and resources because of the difficulty 
of diagnosing autism in the early time and the time consumption of 
diagnosis during clinical appointments; in addition, many electronic 
tests are not recommended due to their risks, thereby making the in-
formation for ASD limited and difficult to collect [5,35] According to 
literature, genes and genetic mutations are considered causes of autism 
disorder Studies differed in identifying and classifying dangerous genes; 
therefore, finding the identification of genes that cause autism is still 
challenging [3,4,12,15,29,32] In conclusion to the above discussion, 
despite the lack of follow-up or corroboration in the literature, these 
findings continue to be an open issue in subsequent literature and have 
shown the lack of investigation triage and/or priority methods based on 
AI for supporting the diagnosis of ASD

level0_chunks.content:
Ac-
cording to the literature analysis and taxonomy, previous studies did not 
cover the roles of MCDM methods in ASD Nevertheless, MCDM tech-
niques can be leveraged in autism disorder to determine the weight of 
ASD criteria and find the important features for this kind of disorder or 
rank the alternative of patients or genes that can be affected on ASD Therefore, this article suggests future research that leverages MCDM 
techniques for ASD, which will be explained in the next section 6.5 Research proposal on potential future direction 
According to the systematic literature review analysis regarding the 
triage of autism patients (Section 4.1), no exclusive study has developed 
MCDM-based approaches that used hybrid solution that can provide 
triage or prioritisation for autism patients according to their severity 
levels In addition, in Section 6.1, no dataset for serving this purpose is 
available Similarly, a comprehensive process is generally lacking to 
recommend the suitable methods for the proposed hybrid approaches Thus, the presented study describes the potential future direction of the 
triage and prioritise methodological aspects for ASD patients based on 
‘medical tests and demographic criteria’ by using integrated MCDM 
methods The hybridised triaging and prioritisation of ASD patients based on 
MCDM solution can be achieved by detecting the health conditions of 
autism patients by categorizing them on the basis of the autism severity 
levels, which represent the triage levels Subsequently, the ASD patients 
(ranking) were prioritised within each triage level Such hybridisation is 
a challenging task and is not reported in literature The evolution of this 
new methodology version should be dependent on a new verified ASD 
dataset, including the ‘medical tests and demographic criteria’ This 
research direction presents an intelligent triage and prioritisation 
framework for diagnosing patients with ASD and can support remote 
triage and prioritisation through telemedicine

13AHP, ANP and BWM methods suffer from inconsistency issues that will 
dramatically increase with the number of criteria in a pairwise com-
parison Thus, the use of one of these methods to evaluate the selected 
medical tests and demographic criteria obtained from FDM is considered 
impractical due to these disadvantages Many comparisons complicate 
the application of the model, especially in the cases of a larger number of 
criteria According to some authors [76], performing completely 
consistent pairwise comparisons in the AHP method is almost impossible 
if more than nine criteria exist This problem is usually surpassed by 
dividing the criteria into sub criteria, which further complicates the 
model This inconsistency problem can be solved by the relatively new 
fuzzy-weighted zero-inconsistency (FWZIC) method [77], which de-
termines the weight coefficients of the criteria with zero inconsistency 
issue regardless of the number of criteria This method depends on the 
differences in the expert preferences per criterion to compute its sig-
nificance level in the decision-making process FWZIC method has been 
presented in different versions [77–79] The variations of the three versions are related to vagueness ’s issues However, the latest version is 
[80], and this study is going to use it For the FDOSM, the latest and powerful method called fuzzy decision 
by opinion score method (FDOSM) based on triangular fuzzy number 
(TFN), which was proposed to consider the idea of an ideal solution, 
avoid two preferences, reduce the number of comparisons, define fair 
and implicit understandable comparisons, prevent inconsistency, reduce 
vagueness and yield a minimum number of mathematical operations 
[81–83] FDOSM applies the idea of ideal solution and opinion matrix 
under a fuzzy environment with fewer mathematical equations FDOSM 
provides logical decisions because it depends on the opinion of the de-
cision matrix (the expert)

level0_chunks.content:
This sys-
tematic review supports the use of machine learning to suggest predic -
tive models that can be involved during autism diagnosis for this triple 
track of interdisciplinary research, namely, ASD diagnosis and gene 
contributions, triage/priority tools and strategies and AI theory solu-
tions The study found that few literatures attempted to find a method 
used to prioritise autistic patients based on clinical triage According to 
the literature, most of the included articles have discussed the issue of 
prioritising autism by studying the affected genes and biomarkers, and 
only few have focused on studying the traditional clinical diagnostic 
methods and attempted to interfere with machine learning approaches 
to accelerate diagnostic patients Scattered efforts on identifying risk 
genes for ASD disease through AI techniques have been exerted in the 
literature Additionally, the ASD triage is still dependent on clinical 
questionnaires without any technological consideration to leverage the 
speed and concise tools that can be provided by AI and ML A surprising 
open issue is that the early diagnosis of young patients (i.e., less than 18 
months of age) with autism remains inconclusive In addition, tele-
medicine applications have a low opportunity to extend outstanding 
solutions for remote monitoring, detection and diagnosis of autism pa-
tients of all ages In terms of triage and priority, this study supports the 
application of AI and machine learning to propose a real-time predictive 
model that could be useful for diagnosing autism via telemedicine ap-
plications Certainly, intelligent triage and prioritisation system are 
essential to detect the severity levels of patients ’ and identify suitable 
patients for telehealth diagnostic applications In this paper, focus has 
been dedicated to the concept of prioritisation and how it can integrate 
autism patients

level1_summaries.node_id: Triage and priority-based healthcare diagnosis using artificial intelligence for autism spectrum disorder and gene contribution- A systematic review _L1_abstract
level1_summaries.content: The study systematically reviews AI methods for diagnosing autism spectrum disorder (ASD), highlighting the tools and strategies used and examining how AI trends contribute to triage and prioritization based on gene contributions. It categorizes the literature into three areas: triage based on diagnosis methods, prioritization for risky genes, and e-triage using telehealth, and suggests a new methodology for future work to improve ASD patient triaging and prioritization using decision-making techniques.

level1_summaries.node_id: Triage and priority-based healthcare diagnosis using artificial intelligence for autism spectrum disorder and gene contribution- A systematic review _L1_introduction
level1_summaries.content: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neuropsychiatric condition with a significant genetic component, affecting 67 million people worldwide, and is more prevalent in males. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as ADOS and ADI-R, are time-consuming, while computer-aided diagnostic tools like EEG and MRI present challenges such as high costs and potential risks. The paper aims to explore the integration of AI techniques to improve the diagnosis of ASD by prioritizing gene sets and addressing current diagnostic challenges.

level1_summaries.node_id: Triage and priority-based healthcare diagnosis using artificial intelligence for autism spectrum disorder and gene contribution- A systematic review _L1_methods
level1_summaries.content: The study conducted a systematic review following established guidelines, collecting literature from multiple databases to examine ASD triage, prioritization, and gene contributions using AI. A Boolean search strategy was employed to gather relevant English-language papers published between 2017 and 2022, focusing on topics such as machine learning, telemedicine, and AI techniques, while excluding papers lacking clear methods for prioritizing and triaging autism cases.

level2_summary.content: The paper addresses the challenge of diagnosing autism spectrum disorder (ASD) by exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in triage and prioritization contexts. Utilizing a systematic review methodology, the study analyzes literature from multiple databases to assess the role of AI in ASD diagnosis and its genetic contributions. The research highlights the benefits and challenges of AI-driven triage, emphasizing its potential to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient prioritization. The findings underscore the significance of AI in enhancing medical decision-making processes for ASD, suggesting improvements in patient outcomes and resource allocation.

for autism spectrum disorder and gene contribution: A systematic review 
Shahad Sabbar Joudara,b, A.S. Albahria,*, Rula A. Hamida,c 
aInformatics Institute for Postgraduate Studies (IIPS), Iraqi Commission for Computers and Informatics (ICCI), Baghdad, Iraq 
bUniversity of Technology, Baghdad, Iraq 
cCollege of Business Informatics, University of Information Technology and Communications (UOITC), Baghdad, Iraq 
ARTICLE INFO 
Keywords: 
Autism 
Artificial intelligence 
Machine learning 
ASD 
Diagnosis 
Telemedicine 
Triage and priority ABSTRACT 
The exact nature, harmful effects and aetiology of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) have caused widespread 
confusion. Artificial intelligence (AI) science helps solve challenging diagnostic problems in the medical field 
through extensive experiments. Disease severity is closely related to triage decisions and prioritisation contexts in 
medicine because both have been widely used to diagnose various diseases via AI, machine learning and auto-
mated decision-making techniques. Recently, taking advantage of high-performance AI algorithms has achieved 
accessible success in diagnosing and predicting risks from clinical and biological data. In contrast, less progress 
has been made with ASD because of obscure reasons. According to academic literature, ASD diagnosis works 
from a specific perspective, and much of the confusion arises from the fact that how AI techniques are currently 
integrated with the diagnosis of ASD concerning the triage and priority strategies and gene contributions. To this 
end, this study sought to describe a systematic review of the literature to assess the respective AI methods using 
the available datasets, highlight the tools and strategies used for diagnosing ASD and investigate how AI trends 
contribute in distinguishing triage and priority for ASD and gene contributions. Accordingly, this study checked 
the Science Direct, IEEE Xplore Digital Library, Web of Science (WoS), PubMed, and Scopus databases. A set of 
363 articles from 2017 to 2022 is collected to reveal a clear picture and a better understanding of all the aca-
demic literature through a final set of 18 articles. The retrieved articles were filtered according to the defined 
inclusion and exclusion criteria and classified into three categories. The first category includes ‘Triage patients 
based on diagnosis methods ’ which accounts for 16.66% (n 3/18). The second category includes ‘Prioritisation 
for Risky Genes ’ which accounts for 66.6% (n 12/18) and is classified into two subcategories: ‘Mutations 
observation based ’, ‘Biomarkers and toxic chemical observations ’. The third category includes ‘E-triage using 
telehealth ’ which accounts for 16.66% (n 3/18). This multidisciplinary systematic review revealed the tax-
onomy, motivations, recommendations and challenges of ASD research that need synergistic attention. Thus, this 
systematic review performs a comprehensive science mapping analysis and discusses the open issues that help 
perform and improve the recommended solution of ASD research direction. In addition, this study critically 
reviews the literature and attempts to address the current research gaps in knowledge and highlights weaknesses 
that require further research. Finally, a new developed methodology has been suggested as future work for 
triaging and prioritising ASD patients according to their severity levels by using decision-making techniques. 
1.Introduction 
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neuropsychiatric disorder that 
affects brain activities at different levels with high evidence of genetic 
contribution. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 67 
million persons are affected with ASD around the world [1]. Autistic 
children manifest many symptoms, such as repetitive behaviour, abnormalities in facial and voice expressions and slow speech learning, 
as well as communication difficulties [2]. These symptoms generally are 
observed during the first two years and tend to be continuous. The 
aetiology of this kind of disorder are varied and unclear, some cases are 
related to gene mutations, such as “de novo or transmitted loss of 
function (LOF) mutations ” [3], or it could be caused by environmental 
toxic involvement in the genetic abnormalities [4]. Some types of autism 
have been inherited from one or both parents. Males could be affected

2with these neurodevelopmental disorders four times more than females 
[5]. As such, autism must be diagnosed at early stages to help limit the 
development of the condition [6]. Therefore, many clinicians depend on 
traditional diagnostic methods, such as Autism Diagnostic Observation 
Schedule (ADOS), to observe the autistic patient behaviour and Autism 
Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R), which takes a long time to com-
plete diagnosis and make decisions. Several computer-aided auxiliary 
diagnostic devices, such as electroencephalogram (EEG), magnetic 
resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT), have been 
utilised for this purpose. The application of CT is not recommended 
because it exposes the patient to potentially harmful ionizing radiation. 
Therefore, the use of this imaging technology requires careful risk 
assessment. In addition, the high cost and time consumption for other 
devices, such as MRI, where a child often needs to be quiet or in a 
general anaesthesia to allow accurate imaging, carry inherent risks [5]. 
Many researchers believed that genes and mutations are highly associ -
ated with ASD, and they still attempted to discover what types and 
priority of gene sets exactly affect autism to obtain an accurate diag-
nosis. This confusion motivated us to shed light on the different trends 
and perspectives and attempted to paint an appropriate picture of how 
to integrate the concepts of triage of ASD, as well as the prioritiation of 
genes that contribute towards the diagnosing of ASD by using AI tech-
niques. Accordingly, the introduction covers three important questions 
according to the scope of our study and provides appropriate answers. 
On the one hand, an early and timely diagnosis is highly associated 
with the triage concept that is based on patients’ prioritisation. Thus, the 
first question that needs to be determined is: ‘What is triage and pri-
oritisation and why is it important for autistic patients?’ 
In medical use, the degrees of urgency of triage is assigned to wounds 
or illnesses to decide the order of treatment for a large number of sick or 
injured people [7]. Triage is a patient’s urgent situation level while the 
prioritisation is ranking patients according to their severity levels [8]. 
The two terms are still confusing and interrelated to each other. How-
ever, the concept of triage is the process used to identify the most urgent 
cases and to determine who should be treated and in what order, 
whereas prioritising is (required) to rank or list a set of things (i.e. pa-
tients, genes, features) in order of priority or importance [9,10]. For 
example, triage could be assigned to patients with four severity levels, 
such as risk, urgent, sick and normal whereas prioritisation can be applied within each severity level to rank patients according to their 
health situation [11]. Thus, for the first procedure, relying on triage in 
clinics is important to determine the ASD patient with the highest ur-
gency needs. For the second procedure, patients can have priority for 
clinical appointment and treatment to cut waiting times and make the 
best use of available resources. The two terms differ slightly in meaning 
but are quite different in medical applications; therefore, this confusion 
needs to be explained, especially in autistic research. 
Triage levels can be assigned for ASD patients who cover different 
levels, such as severe, moderate and mild cases. 
[5]. In addition, patients can be grouped on the basis of a triage using 
a triage-based questionnaire to identify appropriate ASD patients who 
need priority diagnostic evaluation [9]. Although some autism centres, 
such as the Marcus Autism Centre and UMN-AND, opted to prioritise 
patients according to some criteria (e.g. young children, or kids with 
more urgent needs or give a priority to those with additional complex -
ities) that can impact treatment decisions [9]. Besides, the concept of 
prioritising in gene contexts has been widely used to prioritise the list of 
genes that can be a cause of ASD, such as prioritising genes to calculate 
their importance in a “cell-type-specific” [12], which can be etiological 
to ASD. In conclusion, triage and priority tools support for leading 
autism diagnosis, understanding evidence-based diagnosis, which is 
used in ASD medical tests to guide treatment decisions and provide more 
explanations to make the autism medical contexts and its treatment 
more accurate [10]. 
On the other hand, many researchers attempted to leverage AI 
development technology in ASD diagnosis cases; therefore, the second 
question is ‘How can AI contribute to ASD diagnosis?’ 
AI is placed on triage and priority for machines to learn from medical 
experience, adjust to new inputs and perform physician-like tasks [13]. 
Most medical AI applications that are presented today – from heart 
chronic disease, diabetics, Alzheimer’s, etc. – rely heavily on data 
mining, machine learning, natural language processing, intelligent and 
decision making, more. Using these technologies, computers can be 
trained to accomplish triage and prioritisation strategies and/or tasks for 
different ASD directions (e.g., genes priority, patients’ triage, patients’ 
priority) by processing large amounts of autistic data and recognizing 
diagnosis patterns in the data. AI software can be programmed to 
accurately spot signs of a certain ASD in medical images, such as MRIs List of abbreviations

3and CT scans [14]. Existing similar solutions have already been studied 
by researchers to use AI for reducing time and obtaining a concise ASD 
diagnosis. By using such AI tools, clinicians can diagnose patients more 
precisely and prescribe the most suitable healthcare. Amongst others, 
machine learning has been widely used to determine the accuracy 
metrics utilised in diagnosis. According to the literature, several ML 
methods, such as support vector machines (SVM), random forest (RF), 
and others had been used in ASD diagnosis to distinguish the risk ASD 
and non-ASD genes [15,16]. Trends shown in this question are restricted 
to some AI directions, sparse and scattered throughout the ASD litera -
ture. Accordingly, this paper attempts to update the literature on ASD 
diagnosis of ambiguity systematically using AI techniques and associ -
ated concepts of triage and priority. Many of the published reviews have 
been addressed ASD but they are not complementary to AI, triage, pri-
ority and diagnosis in telehealth and/or telemedicine. Therefore, the 
third question is ‘What are the current academic reviews of literature of 
the ASD triage and prioritisation based AI, and what is critical 
analysis?’ 
To determine the current state of academic knowledge about pri-
oritising ASD, the aim of previous studies and limitations should be 
discussed. In Ref. [17], the authors summarised 13 studies where AI is 
used to assess and examine whether other behavioural data can poten -
tially be used to recognize ASD characteristics. Although the machine 
learning algorithms depend on the training dataset, no extensive 
research assesses how the quality of input data can affect the accuracy 
yet. While the ethical issue around data privacy is also another problem 
under debate, reports on AI technology integrated with autism disorder 
issues are not efficient. The survey of [18] discussed how individuals 
with ASD were handled by technology-based intervention methodolo -
gies, including modern computer-aided systems, computer 
vision-assisted technologies and virtual reality. They concluded that a 
gap exists between neuroscience, including autism disorders, psychol -
ogy and the research community of computer science to develop an AI 
technology for ASD individuals. The 31 collected studies conclude that 
clinicians were not convinced in general with technology-based in-
terventions because of the non-empirical nature of results that had been 
published. The major reason is a greater number of studies on distinct 
intervention methodologies does not obey any specific standard or AI 
research design. In Ref. [19], the study aimed to identify and describe 
supervised ML directions in ASD articles and guide researchers in 
expanding their research computationally and statistically towards this 
disease. The limitations they found related to unlabeled data were 
consuming time, cost and effort besides the complicity of some ML 
models. Thus, the researchers must consider if the understanding of 
models is going to be more important than the result when selecting the 
ML model. In conclusion to the above reviews, the authors neglected the 
diagnosis towards the importance of triage and prioritisation in autism 
patients’ life. At this point, to fill up the comparative analyses between 
the presented work and published reviews, Table 1 shows the compar -
ative points and differences. 
As shown in Table 1, most previous works did not cover the main 
aspects that the present study aims to provide. Some reviews covered 
some important aspects but neglected other concepts. In addition, 
different important information in this systematic review is explained 
represented by tables, figures, discussion and analysis considering integration amongst health diagnosis autism, triage and priority in ASD, 
gene contributions, the AI technologies for supporting ASD, and tele-
health/telemedicine application for helping ASD. No such study has 
been presented yet. In this aspect, this study has multifaceted contri -
butions as follows: (1) Constructing new taxonomy to classify the 
available studies for the triage and prioritisation of ASD into three 
distinct categories. (2) Highlights the motivations, challenges, recom -
mendations and open issues and key solutions that need focus to reduce 
the complexity of health autism diagnosis through AI technologies. (3) 
Explain various dataset results and available sources to embrace triage 
and priority for ASD and present useful tables that contain all datasets 
and machine learning methods found in the literature. (4) Offering the 
innovation of our ideas that developed a multi-criteria decision making 
(MCDM)-based used several methods (e.g., Delphi method, IT2TR- 
FWZIC method, and FDOSM) that can provide for triage autism pa-
tients or even prioritise them according to their severity levels. 
2.Method 
This study was formed according to the systematic review guidelines 
showed in (Fig. 1) [20,21] and collected the literatures based on query 
from multiple reliable databases: Science direct (SD), IEEE Xplore digital 
library (IEEE), Web of Science (WoS), PubMed and Scopus databases. 
The collected articles focused on ASD triage and prioritisation and gene 
contributions from different perspectives aided by AI. 
2.1. Search strategy 
This study utilised a Boolean query (conclude OR, AND) to link the 
keywords (‘autism’ OR ‘autistic’) AND (‘triage’ OR ‘prioritisation’ OR 
‘prioritisation’ OR ‘telemedicine’) AND (‘artificial intelligence’ OR 
‘multi-criteria decision making’ OR ‘machine learning’ OR ‘deep 
learning’). The study applied the query to ensure collecting of all related 
papers based on our topic besides promoting the study with other papers 
that focused on how the triage affected the ASD patients. The collected 
articles from databases were published from 2017 to 2022. 
2.2. Inclusion criteria and exclusion criteria 
All written papers in the English language and submitted to confer -
ences or journals were included. The main topics in the studies are 
related to ASD that utilised various topics, such as prioritisation, ranking 
and triage with machine learning algorithms and AI techniques. Papers 
with the telemedicine and telehealth perspectives are also included. The 
exclusion criteria consisted of all papers that were not written in the 
English language. The diagnosis of autism without a clear method, tool, 
strategy and approach for prioritising and triaging cases were also 
excluded. 
3.Comprehensive science mapping analysis 
The application of bibliometric measurements in various fields has 
been increased. Several techniques and software tools have been pro-
posed to implement the scientific mapping analysis of published studies 
of fragmented and controversial streams of research [22–25]. The total

3.1. Annual production 
Fig. 2 shows the relation between the year of publication and annual 
production. Most publications during 2020 were approximately 50% or 
(9/18) papers. Most of the papers focused on prioritising ASD risk genes. 
Followed by the year 2021 were 27.7% or (5/18) of publications during 
the year. Publication papers decreased before 2020 were focused on 
triage and prioritisation of ASD using AI techniques. 
3.2. Country-specific production 
Fig. 3 illustrates the collected articles from seven countries. The ar-
ticles generally included case studies in ASD clinics, and most studies 
were focused on genes depending on the Simons Simplex Collection 
(SSC) of genes, which is known as Simons Foundation Autism Research 
Initiative (SFARI), to provide more understanding and improve the diagnosis of ASD. The highest percentage of studies were from USA 
(50%) or (9/18 papers) followed by China (2/18 papers), Canada (2/18 
papers), Turkey (2/18 papers) whilst each of the following countries 
were published (1/18 paper): Korea, Denmark and Macedonia in the 
field of Triage and prioritisation of ASD using AI technologies. 
3.3. Word cloud 
A word cloud points to the most essential topics that deal with a 
particular subject. Fig. 4 presents the important words adopted by pre-
vious studies on triage-based prioritisation for ASD. Most papers focused 
on the ASD patient ’s aspects (i.e. autism, diagnostic, prioritisation, 
spectrum disorders, genes, mutations and biomarkers). The keywords 
refer to the words that interest the authors who investigated the pri-
oritisation of ASD. High-performance AI techniques in prediction and 
diagnosis have made less progress in diagnosing and prioritising autism 
patients based on triage. The academic literature has presented ASD 
diagnosis work from a specific perspective and much confusion arises 
from the fact that AI theory is currently integrated with ASD diagnosis 
concerning triage and priority.

search query and after using Mendeley application to remove the

(195) articles. A full-text reading to identify the excluded articles has 
been achieved in the eligibility phase to obtain (78) articles. Finally, 
final set articles included (18) papers in the final phase (Included). The 
included studies that were obtained, such as prioritisation of related 
genes, using EEG signals to rank the related features and prioritising 
autism patients based on clinical triage, are close to our scope. AI 
technologies are used to create a more concise algorithm for ASD 
diagnosis and are less time consuming within these articles. In addition, 
the final set articles are divided into three major categories based on the 
aim and objective evidence across studies that fit pre-specified inclusion 
and exclusion criteria. The first category, which contained (n 3/18) 
16.66% articles, is focused on ‘Triage patients based on diagnosis 
methods ’. The second category is focused on ‘Prioritisation for Risky 
Genes ’. This category contained (n 12/18) 66.6% articles and had two 
subcategories. The first sub-category containing (8/12 articles) was the 
‘Mutations Observation based ’, the second sub-category containing (4/ 
12 articles) was the ‘Biomarkers and toxic chemical observations ’. 
Finally, the third category containing (3/18 article) 16.66% was the ‘E- 
triage using telehealth ’. These studies were grouped and formed into the 
taxonomy below (see Fig. 5). 
4.1. Triage patients based on diagnosis methods 
The diagnosis is the first step of any cases, and for ASD, it is essential 
and must be taken early for faster service. Many diagnosis methods were used for the clinical detection of the autistic patients: ADOS, for 
observing the autistic patient behaviour and ADI-R with 93 question 
needs to assess for autism symptomatology. These types of methods 
spend time and cause diagnosis delay, therefore prioritising patients 
based on high urgency for booking to clinical diagnosis is important to 
accelerate the treatment. In total, (n 3/18) articles among the 
screening papers showed triage patients based on ASD diagnosis 
methods according to the collected articles. In Ref. [26], this study used 
machine learning method to predict the subgroups of Korean ASD based 
on Diagnostic Statistical Manual for Mental Disorders-IV Text Revision 
(DSM-IV-TR) and ranks the autism ADI-R diagnostic algorithm items to 
prove that machine learning methods sufficiently predict the diagnosis 
with minimum items. They produced 10 levels of patient prioritisation 
based on two board-certified child psychiatrist triages where they used 
ADI-R, ADOS and clinical interviews. The article in Ref. [5] proposed 
another diagnosis method based on EEG to assist in the automatic 
detection of ASD. A new method for AI has been proposed using CNNs 
that are utilised as deep-learning algorithms to help in the automatic 
detection of ASD and by using a big EEG signal dataset and selecting the 
group of ASD patients to cover all triage levels: mild, moderate and 
severe. They found that signals from children with autism have a com-
mon morphological pattern, which makes them distinguishable from 
normal EEG. The study of [27] integrated the Rapid Interactive 
Screening Test for Autism in Toddlers (RITA-T) using two levels 
screening tools, which were used for improving the triage process for 
those at risk of ASD, by referring them sooner to more appropriately

7evaluation clinics. The RITA-T detected the risky ASD patients for timely 
diagnosis and other health services. An unadjusted Logistic Regression 
(LR) model was utilised to evaluate the relationship between ASD

4.2. Prioritisation for risky genes 
Gene mutations play an essential role in autism problems. Therefore, 
many studies focused on genes for autism patients to determine whether 
specific genes cause this kind of disorders or not. This category contains 
(n 12/18) articles focused on prioritising genes according to their risk 
using some machine learning methods. This category can be classified 
into two subsections, the first focused on mutations that affected ASD 
genes, and the second concentrated on biomarkers and toxic chemical 
observations. 
4.2.1. Mutations observation 
The gene mutation is an alteration in one or more genes, and some of 
these variations can cause genetic disorders like ASD. This subsection 
contains (n 8/12) publications. In Ref. [3], the study mentioned that 
“only a fraction of the hundreds of nominated ASD-related genes have 
identified de novo or transmitted loss of function (LOF) mutations that 
can be directly attributed to the disorder ”. De novo mutations impact 
risk for several diseases and disorders, particularly for ASD [28]. In 
addition, they discussed the importance of prioritisation for ASD 
candidate genes that help in filtering out false-positive results and for 
aiding the researchers to concentrate on genes that are regarded as more 
casualty for this disorder. By leveraging a brain-specific functional 
relationship network (FRN) of genes, the study constructed the machine 
learning model to provide a genome-wide ranking of ASD risk genes to 
differentiate between ASD-related and whom without. In Ref. [15], the 
authors also focused on identified de novo, which probably 
gene-disrupting (DN-LGD) mutations, they found that 353 genes nomi -
nated to autism, where 27 frequent genes likely related to autism, and 
176 negative genes in siblings not affected. They proposed a bioinfor -
matics framework and used network-based deep learning approach 
(PANDA) to prioritise the autism genes across the human genome, by 
using patterns of gene-gene interactions and topological likeness of 
genes in the interaction network. The study presented in Ref. [29] 
focused on detection problem of the risk gene by using machine learning 
and introducing (forecASD) approach. The authors used genome scale 
data as predictors to identify new genes by using similar properties to 
determine ASD risky genes. They found that 44 genes with more than 
one de novo loss-of-function mutations. In Ref. [30], the state-of-the-art 
machine learning approach has been developed to predict the candidate 
long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) related to ASD. The performance of 
the produced model indicates that RNA transcript sequence may have 
relevant information for ASD risk gene prediction. Besides, they used 
models to prioritise a list of human lncRNAs with predictable expression 
signals in the BrainSpan dataset. As a result, they were able to identify 
good candidate lncRNAs and concluded that: some de novo mutations 
and all familiar ASD risk genes signalling proteins may disrupt 
protein-coding genes and have caused ASD. In Ref. [31], the study 
illustrated that to foretell ASD risk genes, machine learning can be 
employed using features from “spatiotemporal gene expression patterns in 
human brain gene-level constraint metrics, and other gene variation features, 
and when and where ASD genes may affect during brain development ”. Their 
process of gene ranking has provided a beneficial resource for priori -
tising ASD candidate genes and diagnosing the patients. The study of 
[32] aimed to investigate whether machine learning can help in the 
discovery and diagnosis of disease genes. Therefore, they collected 13 
published ASD gene prioritisation research and evaluated their perfor -
mance using recognised and unfamiliar high-confidence ASD genes. 
They found that machine learning methods which do not incorporate genetic information have restricted benefit for prioritisation of ASD 
danger genes. Their results elucidate that despite utilizing the complex 
data and developed algorithms, the Guilt by association (GBA) machine 
learning model for ASD had failed to outperform genetic measures of 
this type of disease gene. The study of [33] discovering the contribution 
of non-coding mutations to illness using the deep learning-based 
framework to predict the particulate effects and harmful impact of ge-
netic variants. They proposed a new approach to deep learning for 
quantitatively defining the effect of noncoding mutations on transcrip -
tional and post-transcriptional regulation. Their proposed framework of 
genomics predictive had been clarified the role of non-coding mutations 
in ASDs and mutations prioritisation as well. The authors in the article 
[19] tried to “investigate the genes and molecular mechanisms associ -
ated with the occurrence of seizures in ASD ”. They accomplished gene 
prioritisation by using five propagation algorithms: “simple random 
walk, heat kernel diffusion, PageRank with priors, HITS with priors, and 
K-step Markov ”. 
4.2.2. Biomarkers and toxic chemical observations 
The aim of autism research on genetic and chemical aetiology is: to 
find out the validated biomarkers, for facilitating the early autism 
diagnosis, prediction of healing response, pursuing progression, evalu -
ating risk, and medical development. This subsection contains (n 4/ 
12) articles. Besides, studies in this subsection focused on how bio-
markers and toxic chemicals can take place in ASD. The cause of many 
mental disorders like ASD is exposure to environmental toxicants (like 
mercury, toluene, lead, PCBs, and arsenic). In Ref. [2], they used signal 
processing and machine learning methods that integrated to analyse 
“microarray gene expression data from homogeneous groups of children 
diagnosed with classic autism, excluding the autism with regression and 
high-functioning autism ’s syndrome ”. The major focus of this paper was 
gene expression pre-processing, which depending on Fractional Fourier 
Transformation, and the acquired data are also utilised for selecting 
biomarkers (the most informative genes). The study of [4] proposed a 
new multi label classification (MLC) model to determine the autism 
risky genes and toxic chemicals on an extensive dataset. The article 
proposed a CNN-based MLC framework to prioritise the autistic risky 
genes and chemical toxicity that is causative and its subtypes. In 
Ref. [12], the study constructed predictive models to promote the ASD 
diagnosis and cell type specific ASD-associated genes and gene sets 
prioritisation that can help as biomarkers for ASD. They studied the 
importance of genes in the cell type-specific predictive model through 
prioritising of genes. In Ref. [34], the study produced a predictive so-
lution for ASD risk genes to identify the temporospatial regions of the 
brain structures at different developmental time points. The study aimed 
to explore the specificity of ASD gene expression in the brain for helping 
diagnosis and detection in possible ASD in the future. They prioritised 
the temporospatial features based on their accuracy in prediction 
contribution; therefore, they identified top ten ranked temporospatial 
regions related in ASD aetiology. 
4.3. E-triage using telehealth 
The E-Triage system is essential for identifying which patients are 
appropriate for telemedicine or book for clinical visit and prioritising 
patients according to their high urgency needs. In this category, the 
triage of autistic patients through telemedicine techniques has been 
focused and discussed. In Ref. [10], the study suggested that telehealth 
consulting in diagnosis and early intervention systems could have a 
positive impact for diagnosis evaluation and the ability of caregivers and 
families to schedule appointments and clinical visits as well. In Ref. [9], 
this study aimed to provide instances about how autism clinical centres 
adjusted their traditional approaches to conduct their diagnosis assess -
ment for ASD during any pandemic like Covid-19 and how shared their 
challenges to other centres for benefit. They suggest that all patients 
would be triaged based on their high urgency need for booking on two S.S. Joudar et al.

second one for visiting with a licensed psychologist. In the study of [35], 
a new mobile-health screening tool has been developed by Cognoa, their

5.Discussion 
In this section, three important aspects of the literature behind the 
triage procedure and priority contexts, namely, motivations, challenges, 
and limitations of using AI and recommendations, are discussed to 
mitigate these difficulties to improve triage and prioritisation of 
patients. 
5.1. Motivations for ASD triage and prioritisation 
This section discusses the advantages of triage and prioritisation 
reported in the academic literature. Three main benefits can be identi -
fied from the collected articles as follows: 
≡The triage and prioritisation concepts can reduce cost and time 
consumption to provide an early diagnosis for autism patients. The 
conventional clinical diagnosis of autism using ADOS requires be-
tween 60 and 90 min for initial DSM-IV-TR assessment, due to 
variation in reliability between residents [16] and the ADI-R 
assessment of autistic symptoms. Each patient needs more than 2 h 
to complete the triage and/or priority process. For this, the authors of 
[26] applied “top-ranking items for ASD diagnosis in the Korean 
population ” and can reduce the time to ASD diagnosis. They pro-
duced 10 levels of patient prioritisation based on two board-certified 
child psychiatrist triage where they used ADI-R, ADOS and clinical 
interviews. Also, the long waiting time for service, clinical appoint -
ments and higher costs are improved. Accordingly, several studies 
attempted to overcome these issues to reduce the cost and time 
consumption for diagnosis. To overcome the expensive and time 
consumption in the process of genetic and genomic studies were 
usually performed to identify ASD risk genes and numerous gener -
ated potentials nominated genes, and difficulty in validation as well. 
Therefore, a study [12] constructed a predictive model that could 
promote the diagnosis of autism and prioritised cell-type-specificity 
that could be used as potential biomarkers of ASD. The machine 
learning algorithms can identify and predict the genes involved in 
the disorder better than depending only on unclear traditional ge-
netics that consume time in diagnosis [32]. Understanding the as-
sociation of genes related to the disorder/disease aids better 
diagnosis and treatments which is better than costly experiments and 
time-consuming during the evaluation of the genes [15]. Triage 
process for children with ASD can help sooner by referring them to 
clinical appointments for ASD evaluation and can reduce the wait 
times for both types of children (who have the ASD risk and one’s 
non ASD risk) [10,27,35]. In conclusion to the above benefits from 
reducing cost and time consumption, the triage and priority can 
identify ASD risk and nominated genes, leverage machine learning in 
reducing time and cost during ASD diagnosis, and understand the 
association of genes related to the disorder to obtain diagnosis. 
≡The triage and prioritisation can improve therapeutic strategies and 
aid autism patients with daily activities. Determining “the brain 
temporospatial regions where the risk genes are expressed in ASD 
patients ” could improve the therapeutic strategies for better 
healthcare and treatment for ASD risky patients [34]. Besides, 
releasing the association of genes for ASD patients through priority 
tools helps in designing therapeutic strategies and better diagnostic 
situations [15]. ≡Triage and prioritisation focusing on autism case evaluations, which 
are important to identify the appropriate treatment for patients and 
prioritise the certain patients considered ‘urgent ’ than other ASD 
patients with less symptoms. The evaluation of the status of each ASD 
patient, which prompts the clinicians to consider and implement 
diagnostic processes innovatively to adapt the situation and serve the 
patients ’ need,is essential during Covid-19 and any pandemics [9]. 
5.2. Challenges for ASD triage and prioritisation 
Several concerns detailed in studies related to diagnosis, prioritising 
and triage patients are shown in (Fig. 6). The identification of all risky 
genes that contribute to ASD risk are still concerning, and no standard 
set of risky genes has been identified [15,29,32]. Although many studies 
attempted to determine them, they overlook potentially instrumental 
mutations with small to medium effect sizes [3]. No laboratory of neu-
roimaging tests or even any biochemical markers can currently be uti-
lised as a diagnostic standard for ASD [4]. “The causal variants and the 
specific cell types in which the diseases-risk variants may be active are 
unclear ” [12]. A strong clue of clinical and genetic overlap was observed 
between ASD and other types of neurodevelopmental disorders and 
represented by a spectrum of disorders, such as overlapping with epi-
lepsy or high-functioning autism [2,31]. The age of patients that is 
covered has a gap due to the limited available data for ages including 
31–48 months of age [35]. However, the evidence level of using EEG 
monitoring has not yet reached the recommended level for diagnostic or 
even screening of all ASD [5]. The improvement of identification of ASD 
earlier is still concerning for clinical, besides, the limitation of ASD 
clinicians, causes overwhelming, due to the volume of referrals, thereby 
enabling patients to get much time until evaluations [27]. The prioriti -
sation may vary according to the availability of human equipment and 
resources, as well as some policies that are sensitive to domestic prob-
lems in contrast to the goal of ASD evaluations [9]. In conclusion, four 
main challenges were encountered: there is an ambiguity of identifica -
tion of risk genes, and the overlapping with other neurodevelopmental 
disorders could be an open issue. The data limitations are still a valid 
concern, especially for the lack of medical and laboratory data, besides 
the issues of early diagnosis and poor supplementary services (Fig. 6). 
5.3. Recommendations for ASD triage and prioritisation 
This section illustrates the recommendations of all collected studies 
that are related to the prioritisation and triage concepts, as well as 
several future opportunities to evaluate the tools related to ASD, 
including studies for improving the accuracy of standard assessment 
tools. 
≡Recommendations to implement the proposed models : Some 
studies constructed predictive models for autistic diagnosis and 
others ranked their results, such as prioritised finding risky genes and 
recommended to replicate their finding for future work. Researchers 
mentioned their constructed predictive models for promoting the 
diagnosis of ASD and may use the “cell type-specific ASD-associated 
genes and gene sets” as prospective biomarkers of ASD [12]. Other 
study recommended replicating their findings (the Rapid Interactive 
Screening Test for Autism in Toddlers) by other researchers for 
various populations of children and families with autism [27]. Novel 
genetic approaches involved in neurodevelopment disorders is 
highly recommended to help and support autism research [34]. The 
whole genome ranking had been proposed as a useful resource for 
ASD gene discovery effort [3]. The study constructed a novelty of 
identifying ASD risk genes and toxic chemicals that can lead to better 
healthcare decisions [4]. Another study proposed as a starting point 
to produce new suggestions to investigate presently appreciated in 
the molecular aetiology of autism [29]. Hybrid deep lightweight 
features extracted from EEG signals are used and intended to be S.S. Joudar et al. 

Computers in Biology and Medicine 146 (2022) 105553
9applied in the future for the early detection of ASD in clinics [5]. As a 
testing instrument for ASD, a proposed study (Cognoa) has potential 
psychometric advantages that may aid in maximizing the identifi -
cation of likely ASD cases and minimizing false positives. Therefore, 
the resources can be allocated efficiently, and young children can 
receive early intervention services [35]. 
≡Recommendation to investigate ASD risky genes: According to 
literature, no specific risky gene set finding is attained yet, but 
several studies had classified some genes as risky and contributed in 
autism. In Ref. [31], the authors recommended further investigating 
needs in the future to determine whether their ranked gene system 
can be specified only for ASD. The study of [32] focused on 
“developing and validating statistical models for genetic association, 
specifically for the association between rare variants and disease ”, to 
discover illness genes. 
≡Recommendations to utilize AI for ASD diagnosis : The AI can 
provide a quick diagnosis in medical science before the final diag-
nostic, which depends on expert decision [26]. The use of sophisti -
cated modelling and learning algorithms is highly recommended to 
remarkably describe the genetic architecture of complicated disor -
ders and diseases [12,15]. 
≡Recommendations for data availability: The data limitation can 
slow down the development of research in specific fields. The “high- 
quality gene expression profiles ” must be more available publicly in 
the future to facilitate accurate developing models for autism risk 
gene prediction [30,34]. 
6.ASD: critical analysis and research gaps 
This study conducts a comprehensive analysis of scientific mapping 
and discusses current state and open issues that aid in the imple -
mentation and improvement of the recommended solution of the ASD 
research direction. No clear identification of the contribution of AI, 
intelligent decision-making and machine learning is provided to eval-
uate and prioritise autism patients according to their health severity. 
However, most studies have only focused on prioritising risk genes, and 
no clear method has been applied to assign proper weights to gene types 
or even to identify influential genes in the context of intelligent decision- 
making methods. The integration of medical tests and demographic 
criteria can play a vital role in the detection of triage severity levels, and 
minimal attention has been paid to the prioritisation solution for the 
autism patients. In addition, no attempts have been made to develop a 
clinical triage method for ASD patients. Five complex and important 
open issues associated with the current topic of this study are stated in 
this section. 
6.1. Available ASD datasets and resources 
Several studies have focused on prioritising ASD-risk genes based on 
the online dataset (SFARI Genes) that classified many genes associated with autism, that is, from high-confidence genes to syndrome. Other 
studies focused on examining ASD patients according to clinical diag-
nostic measures, such as ADOS and ADI-R [26,27] or by using EEG [5] to 
collect data (Table 2). 
As shown in Table 2, the studies of [3,15,29–32] used SFARI genes as 
high confidence. In Ref. [14], the study used 65 reported genes from 
Ref. [36]. In addition, the true negative genes from non-ASD genes were 
created by Ref. [37], and these genes were related to non-mental dis-
eases. In Ref. [32], the study has also used the second high-confidence 
ASD risky gene set compiled from three extensive Transmission and 
De Novo Association Analysis (TADA) studies [36,39,40]. The study of 
[29] added 1000 genes that are not listed in the SAFRI gene database as 
negative examples. In Ref. [34], the dataset contained 13 developmental 
stages, from 8 weeks to 8 years, collected from 26 brain structures that 
were reported in BrainSpan atlas, the data consisted 732 samples that 
were risk genes of ASD 366 and non-ASD genes 366 on different 
time points of 26 brain structures and developmental stages. In 
conclusion, 10 out of 12 studies have been focused on gene datasets. 
These studies are depending on either genetic or social databases. 
ASD refers to a mental disorder. It can also have social aetiologies. 
Thus, a sociodemographic dataset that consists of medical and social 
criteria that influence ASD have not been used in terms of triage and 
priority for autism patients. The affected criteria that can be used for 
ASD needs more investigation. In addition, no study uses medical and 
laboratory test criteria for the triage and prioritisation of patients [10, 
26]. Laboratory and clinical data, such as D3, B12, Zinc, T3, T4, TSH, 
GSE, patient ’s blood type, maternal blood type and father ’s blood group, 
need to be considered [42,43]. 
6.2. Application of used traditional machine learnings and deep learning 
AI science is implemented with multidisciplinary studies that aid to 
build more precise results. Thus, several articles in autism utilised ma-
chine learning methods (Table 3). 
Study [3] trained and optimized five different ML models: SVM with 
linear kernel, RF, extremely randomized trees, bagging ensemble of RF 
and AdaBoost ensemble of RF. The training approach consisted of 
stratified fivefold cross-validation with a nested grid-search. In 
Ref. [30], different ML algorithms, including SVM, RF and logistic 
regression (LR), were tested. The developmental brain gene expression 
profiles and RNA transcript sequence compositions were used as features 
for model construction to predict and prioritise ASD-associated candi -
date lncRNA. In Study [15], the authors proposed a bioinformatics 
framework by using PANDA and the prioritisation of autism genes with 
the comparison of PANDA ’s measure precision with SVM, RF and LGP 
being presented. Another study of [27] has used RITA-T to identify those 
at risk for ASD in a timely ASD diagnosis evaluation and other services. 
The RITA-T is highly correlated with autism diagnostic measures, 
including the ADOS-2, DSM-5 criteria for ASD and clinician judgment. 
In conclusion, machine learning has been widely used to determine

6.3. Gene contributions towards machine learning 
Gene is a basic functional and physical unit of inheritance where 
deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) was represented as a molecular repository 
of genes that encodes the structure of a gene product, either RNA or 
protein [57]. Meanwhile, a gene mutation corresponds to a modification 
in one or more genes. Some mutations can lead to genetic disorders or 
illnesses [58]. Therefore, many scholars researched the effectiveness of 
genes and mutations on ASD. The ASD is extremely heritable with the 
association of several genetic syndromes, such as ‘Fragile X and Rett 
syndrome ’ [4]. Accordingly, several studies found that the de novo or 
transmitted loss of function (LOF) mutations could disrupt 
protein-coding genes and were regarded as ASD aetiology [30]. Several 
studies leverage machine learning approaches for prioritising 
high-confidence gene candidates in ASD. The enhanced implementation 
of effective interventions to predict the highest confidence gene sets that 
affect ASD [12]. Accordingly, AI tools and methods play a vital role in 
revealing many risky genes that may contribute to ASD [59]. According

6.4. Gap analysis directions 
This study aims to show the importance of prioritisation based on 
specific triage for patients who suffer from ASD and how AI can aid in 
this field. The literature that are collected on the basis our taxonomy can 
offer certain advantages. Firstly, most of the collected studies focused on 
reducing cost and time consumption, which are important for early 
diagnosis to help families from waiting a long time to be served [10,12, 
15,26,27,32,35]. Meanwhile, another study focused on improving 
therapeutic strategy, which is essential for enhancing the healthcare of 
patients [34,60,61]. The evaluation of autism patients is important for 
their prioritisation according to the urgency of their needs where triaged 
based on specialists decisions [9]. The study also showed some concern 
according to literature. The diagnosis of autism remains challenging 
itself due to highly overlapping ASD with other neurodevelopmental 
disorders, such as high-functioning autism and epilepsy [2,31]. Another 
concern is the limitation of data and resources because of the difficulty 
of diagnosing autism in the early time and the time consumption of 
diagnosis during clinical appointments; in addition, many electronic 
tests are not recommended due to their risks, thereby making the in-
formation for ASD limited and difficult to collect [5,35]. According to 
literature, genes and genetic mutations are considered causes of autism 
disorder. Studies differed in identifying and classifying dangerous genes; 
therefore, finding the identification of genes that cause autism is still 
challenging [3,4,12,15,29,32]. In conclusion to the above discussion, 
despite the lack of follow-up or corroboration in the literature, these 
findings continue to be an open issue in subsequent literature and have 
shown the lack of investigation triage and/or priority methods based on 
AI for supporting the diagnosis of ASD. To examine new diagnosis 
technologies and provide researchers with a clear vision of the triage 
and priority tools, we must first be aware of the approaches and existing 
limitations applied, as well as the factors and its weights, available 
dataset types and the recommended machine learning methods in this 
line of ASD. If this requirement is considered, then the construction of 
the diagnosis model is expected to enable physicians and medical staff to 
eventually analyse serial measurements in global ASD medical research. 
The research was analysed from three perspectives (e.g., triage of pa-
tients, priority patients and genetic contributions) based on whether the study followed any of these trends (Table 5). 
As a conclusion from Table 5, a huge gap is found in triage based on 
genes. The collected articles have not focused on the triage concept. 
Meanwhile, most of the studies were concentrated on prioritising genes 
to identify the ASD gene set. In Table 5, the prioritisation based on pa-
tients approached together with triage based on patients due to the 
related context between triage and prioritisation and the important 
benefits of two principles for patients’ diagnosis and treatment. Ac-
cording to the literature analysis and taxonomy, previous studies did not 
cover the roles of MCDM methods in ASD. Nevertheless, MCDM tech-
niques can be leveraged in autism disorder to determine the weight of 
ASD criteria and find the important features for this kind of disorder or 
rank the alternative of patients or genes that can be affected on ASD. 
Therefore, this article suggests future research that leverages MCDM 
techniques for ASD, which will be explained in the next section. 
6.5. Research proposal on potential future direction 
According to the systematic literature review analysis regarding the 
triage of autism patients (Section 4.1), no exclusive study has developed 
MCDM-based approaches that used hybrid solution that can provide 
triage or prioritisation for autism patients according to their severity 
levels. In addition, in Section 6.1, no dataset for serving this purpose is 
available. Similarly, a comprehensive process is generally lacking to 
recommend the suitable methods for the proposed hybrid approaches. 
Thus, the presented study describes the potential future direction of the 
triage and prioritise methodological aspects for ASD patients based on 
‘medical tests and demographic criteria’ by using integrated MCDM 
methods. 
The hybridised triaging and prioritisation of ASD patients based on 
MCDM solution can be achieved by detecting the health conditions of 
autism patients by categorizing them on the basis of the autism severity 
levels, which represent the triage levels. Subsequently, the ASD patients 
(ranking) were prioritised within each triage level. Such hybridisation is 
a challenging task and is not reported in literature. The evolution of this 
new methodology version should be dependent on a new verified ASD 
dataset, including the ‘medical tests and demographic criteria’. This 
research direction presents an intelligent triage and prioritisation 
framework for diagnosing patients with ASD and can support remote 
triage and prioritisation through telemedicine. The conceptual meth -
odology for the proposed work can be shown in Fig. 7.

methods were combined to propose our innovation that will benefit ASD 
patients. The justification behind the use of these methods can be dis-
cussed as follows. 
For the FDM, this method is derived from the traditional Delphi

experts. As such, fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) allows experts to provide 
their views consistently [65]. FDM operates by fuzzy statistics or by 
continuous mathematically explicit membership functions to steady the 
iterative process. This method is useful in unifying ASD criteria and 
establishing importance levels so they can be identified best when 
assessing medical tests and demographic criteria.

13AHP, ANP and BWM methods suffer from inconsistency issues that will 
dramatically increase with the number of criteria in a pairwise com-
parison. Thus, the use of one of these methods to evaluate the selected 
medical tests and demographic criteria obtained from FDM is considered 
impractical due to these disadvantages. Many comparisons complicate 
the application of the model, especially in the cases of a larger number of 
criteria. According to some authors [76], performing completely 
consistent pairwise comparisons in the AHP method is almost impossible 
if more than nine criteria exist. This problem is usually surpassed by 
dividing the criteria into sub criteria, which further complicates the 
model. This inconsistency problem can be solved by the relatively new 
fuzzy-weighted zero-inconsistency (FWZIC) method [77], which de-
termines the weight coefficients of the criteria with zero inconsistency 
issue regardless of the number of criteria. This method depends on the 
differences in the expert preferences per criterion to compute its sig-
nificance level in the decision-making process. FWZIC method has been 
presented in different versions [77–79]. The variations of the three versions are related to vagueness ’s issues. However, the latest version is 
[80], and this study is going to use it. 
For the FDOSM, the latest and powerful method called fuzzy decision 
by opinion score method (FDOSM) based on triangular fuzzy number 
(TFN), which was proposed to consider the idea of an ideal solution, 
avoid two preferences, reduce the number of comparisons, define fair 
and implicit understandable comparisons, prevent inconsistency, reduce 
vagueness and yield a minimum number of mathematical operations 
[81–83]. FDOSM applies the idea of ideal solution and opinion matrix 
under a fuzzy environment with fewer mathematical equations. FDOSM 
provides logical decisions because it depends on the opinion of the de-
cision matrix (the expert). FDOSM can mostly overcome inconsistency, 
which is the main problem in the human approach, and shortens the 
time consumed when performing comparisons. Therefore, this method 
saves data and provides a logical decision. Moreover, normalization and 
the weight in mathematical approach problems are surpassed. The

147.Conclusion 
The implication of this study will offer relevant information to 
practitioners, the healthcare sector and physicians about the works 
involved in the diagnosis of ASD and the impact of AI technique in 
developing and providing accurate triage and priority tools. This sys-
tematic review supports the use of machine learning to suggest predic -
tive models that can be involved during autism diagnosis for this triple 
track of interdisciplinary research, namely, ASD diagnosis and gene 
contributions, triage/priority tools and strategies and AI theory solu-
tions. The study found that few literatures attempted to find a method 
used to prioritise autistic patients based on clinical triage. According to 
the literature, most of the included articles have discussed the issue of 
prioritising autism by studying the affected genes and biomarkers, and 
only few have focused on studying the traditional clinical diagnostic 
methods and attempted to interfere with machine learning approaches 
to accelerate diagnostic patients. Scattered efforts on identifying risk 
genes for ASD disease through AI techniques have been exerted in the 
literature. Additionally, the ASD triage is still dependent on clinical 
questionnaires without any technological consideration to leverage the 
speed and concise tools that can be provided by AI and ML. A surprising 
open issue is that the early diagnosis of young patients (i.e., less than 18 
months of age) with autism remains inconclusive. In addition, tele-
medicine applications have a low opportunity to extend outstanding 
solutions for remote monitoring, detection and diagnosis of autism pa-
tients of all ages. In terms of triage and priority, this study supports the 
application of AI and machine learning to propose a real-time predictive 
model that could be useful for diagnosing autism via telemedicine ap-
plications. Certainly, intelligent triage and prioritisation system are 
essential to detect the severity levels of patients ’ and identify suitable 
patients for telehealth diagnostic applications. In this paper, focus has 
been dedicated to the concept of prioritisation and how it can integrate 
autism patients. The prioritisation of patients based on medical triage 
can be an important method to be applied in telemedicine to obtain a 
quick and specific diagnosis and therapy if possible. Prioritising patients 
based on their urgent needs, is remarkable for early diagnosis and 
treatment. However, no decision-making method can be leveraged to 
prioritise ASD patients based on triage yet. Therefore, this study pro-
posed the use of decision-making techniques for ASD patients to 
leverage from the advantages and implications of MCDM methods (e.g., 
Delphi method, IT2TR-FWZIC method and FDOSM) to determine the 
important features of ASD for triaging and prioritising patients accord -
ing to their severity levels.

The initial search yields a large number of records, which are then screened for eligibility based on pre-defined criteria. Duplicate records are removed. visual_elements.content: The figure displays a flowchart that illustrates the conceptual methodology phases for ASD Triage based on prioritization. It is separated into three phases. Phase 1, labeled 'Collecting and Preprocessing of ASD Dataset', involves collecting medical tests and demographic data, as well as dataset preprocessing and handling missing data. Phase 2, 'Development of new Triage Method for ASD Patients', includes the Fuzzy Delphi Method for selecting criteria, IT2TR-FWZIC Method for weighting criteria, and processes for triaging autism patients. Phase 3, 'Prioritization framework for ASD Patients', uses the Intuitionistic FDOSM Method and prioritizes ASD patients within each triage level based on medical tests, demographic criteria, and patients' lists. Each Triage level is denoted as DM1 (Triage Level 1), DM2 (Triage Level 2) and DM n (Triage Level n).
